answer.rationale:
The binding constraint is not cost, it is the 14-day expiry against a line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. Any action that does not secure continuity of supply this cycle risks a lapse, and a lapse is unrecoverable within the review window. That rules out defer_decision (memory_c5 describes a non-critical service on month-to-month fallback, which this is not) and makes add_second_source (memory_c3) a next-cycle item rather than this one, even though single-source concentration is the real structural exposure.

I am spending the one verification on memory_c2 because it is the only memory that could justify overriding the risk constraint: if switching primary really did cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding, that is the single path that hits the 18% mandate outright. I need the source record to see the conditions under which that onboarding was 'quick' - specifically whether there was volume headroom, a longer runway than 14 days, and qualification already complete. My prior is that it was not executed at 94% utilization against a hard expiry, in which case the memory is true but not transferable to this situation, and switching becomes a delivery-risk bet dressed as a cost decision.

Absent that, I renew with the incumbent to hold the line stable (memory_c1) and structure the renewal as a multi-year volume commitment, which is the one price lever memory_c6 says worked and which is distinct from the in-cycle price reopen the incumbent already refused. memory_c4's benchmarking leverage is largely spent given that refusal.

Uncertainty I am not resolving: memory_c6 is unverified, and I do not know whether the volume pricing there was contingent on volumes or a market position we no longer hold, or whether the incumbent's refusal already extends to term-length restructuring. So I expect this to deliver part of the 18%, not all of it.

Downstream risk to flag explicitly: a multi-year commitment deepens single-source dependency and consumes the flexibility that would fund a second source later, so the concentration exposure in memory_c3 gets worse before it gets better. Anyone reading this next cycle should treat second-sourcing as the priority item and should not read this renewal as evidence that single-sourcing was judged acceptable - it was the least-bad move under a 14-day clock.
